title: Man. Post. Cap. IV: triple life from plural חיים — weak; singular uses; brutes
pass_a_gloss: Beginning the matter from the egg, as they say, you observe that God breathed into man the breath of a triple life—animal, which is of the body through the union of the soul vivifying it; spiritual, which is of the soul through the union of the Holy Spirit sanctifying it; and blessed, which is of soul and body through union with God rendering both blessed. And this you prove by this one argument, because the Hebrew text has in the plural Number חַיִּים lives. Which seems to me most weak: for that plural is everywhere used for the singular, for that one life which you call animal: the examples are ready to hand: see Gen. 3:14 & 23:1 & 25:7, 17 & 27:45; Ps. 17:14 & 31:11; Eccles. 2:17 & 9:9; and elsewhere everywhere. Indeed for that imperfect life such as belongs to brutes, as Gen. 7:15, 22, in which places even to brute animals is attributed נִשְׁמַת חַיִּים the breath, as you speak, of lives, and yet, I think, no life other than the animal, and indeed destitute of reason.
pass_b_english: Starting from the beginning, as they say, you hold that God breathed into man the breath of a threefold life: animal life of the body through the soul's union that keeps it alive; spiritual life of the soul through the Holy Spirit's union that sanctifies it; and blessed life of soul and body through union with God that beats both. Your one proof is that the Hebrew text has the plural חַיִּים, "lives."

That seems to me a very weak prop. The plural is used everywhere for the singular—for that one life you call animal. The examples lie ready: Gen. 3:14; 23:1; 25:7, 17; 27:45; Ps. 17:14; 31:11; Eccles. 2:17; 9:9; and many more. Indeed Gen. 7:15, 22 give even brute animals נִשְׁמַת חַיִּים, the "breath of lives" as you would say—and yet, I think, no life but the animal one, and that without reason.
source_text: Rem ab ovo ut aiunt exorsus observas, Deum inspirasse homini spiraculum triplicis vitae, animalis, quae est corporis per unionem animae illud vivificantis, spiritualis, quae est animae per unionem Spiritus sancti illam sanctificantis, & beatae, quae est animae & corporis per unionem cum Deo utrumque beatum reddentis. Idque hoc uno argumento probas, quia textus hebraeus habet in plurali Numero חַיִּים vitas. Quod mihi videtur debilissimum: passim enim usurpatur plurale illud pro singulari, pro ea una vita, quam tu animalem vocas: obvia sunt exempla: vide Gen. 3. 14. & 23. 1. & 25. 7. 17. & 27. 45. Ps. 17. 14. & 31. 11. Eccles. 2. 17. & 9. 9. Et passim alibi. Immo pro ea imperfecta, qualis est brutorum ut Gen. 7. 15. 22. quibus locis etiam brutis animantibus tribuitur נִשְׁמַת חַיִּים spiraculum, ut tu loqueris, vitarum, nec tamen, opinor, alia vita quam animalis, & quidem destituta ratione.

choices.choice: Reject triple-life proof from Hebrew plural; cite singular and brute uses
choices.why: Cuts sole argument for triple life
